note: Twelve Mutopia engravings, one row per piece. tools/build-piano.mjs fetches each piece's .rdf and .ly, reads the licence and the maintainer out of the .rdf rather than trusting anything written here, and reads the notes out of the .ly. Nothing under data/piano/pieces-*.json is typed by hand.

grading.source: The Royal Conservatory Piano Syllabus, 2022 Edition
grading.note: ABRSM refused the fetch twice, so every level here is RCM's. A null level means RCM does not list the piece, and the row says why.

upstream.note: Mutopia licences each piece separately, so the licence is per file and never per composer. The generator maps the .rdf tag to an SPDX id from a closed table and stops on a tag it does not know.

reader.note: The reader is deliberate about refusing. A bar is kept only when it carries no chord, no polyphony block, no grace note, no tuplet and no ottava bracket, and only when its written durations add up to the time signature exactly. Anything else is dropped and counted, so a piece the reader cannot follow ships as a named gap rather than as a guess.
reader.voice: The staff whose notes are read. It is named per piece because the sources do not agree on a name.
reader.key: Optional, and only where the engraving declares the relative major of the key the piece is actually in. A key signature names two keys and a .ly file records one of them; the generator checks that an override counts the same number of sharps or flats as the engraving, so it can correct the name and never the signature.
reader.rest: A bar carrying a rest is refused. The reader counts a rest toward the bar and the drawing module draws only notes, so such a bar reaches the screen a beat or two short under a page that promises the written durations add up. Seven bars across three pieces go this way, and they come back the day a rest can be drawn.
reader.context: The variable holding the piece's key and time signature when they are not inside the voice itself.
